title: Tool-trust walk gaps: shebang interpreter, shared libraries, and the full PATH given to the child
description: Finding 6 of the opum-ai/ward-cli#308 Opus review, outside DEC-262 (a10) as ruled. The walk covers the resolved tpm2_* path to its final regular file and every ancestor. It does not cover (1) the interpreter named by a script tool shebang, (2) the shared libraries a tool loads, or (3) the PATH the child receives: runTool gives the full search path, so a trusted tool that execs a helper by name bypasses the walk. Needs a design decision from opum-doc before code: walk the shebang interpreter, restrict the child PATH to the walked tool directories, or accept and record the residual. Raise as an A/B through the leader; do not decide here.
implementationNotes:
RULING DEC-262 (a12) from opum-doc, relayed by the leader, VERBATIM. It STARTS ONLY AFTER MONDAY 2026-11-09 PLAN APPROVAL; no code before then. Order: this task is its own PR (with an Opus review) BEFORE slice 2b part 2 (seal/unseal); no real key is piped until it lands.

"1. Built environment: the child gets an environment Ward builds; it does not inherit the parent's. PATH = the resolved tool's directory + /usr/bin + /bin, and every directory in it must pass the (a10)/(a11) walk, or Ward refuses tool_untrusted naming that directory. Only Ward-set variables are passed (TPM2TOOLS_*, the TCTI Ward chooses), plus LANG/LC_ALL=C. No LD_*, no DYLD_*, and not the parent's PATH or HOME.
2. Shebang: if the final file starts with "#!", the interpreter must be an absolute path that passes the walk, or Ward refuses tool_untrusted naming it. "#!/usr/bin/env X" is accepted only by walking env; rule 1 confines X to walked directories. A relative interpreter is refused.
3. Shared libraries: a recorded residual, not built. Rule 1 removes LD_PRELOAD and LD_LIBRARY_PATH. An ELF RUNPATH pointing at a directory another user can write is a packaging defect outside AC2; note it in the threat-model ADR, and do not parse ELF.
Tests, both directions. Accept: a symlinked multicall install, run with the built environment. Reject: an interpreter in a writable directory; a relative interpreter; a helper that is findable only on the parent's PATH.
Order: WCLI-164 is its own PR before 2b part 2 (seal/unseal), with an Opus review. No real key is piped until it lands."

RULING DEC-262 (a13) from opum-doc, relayed by the leader, VERBATIM; applied to #313 as a follow-up commit.

"- If the interpreter named in a tool's "#!" line is itself a "#!" script, Ward refuses with tool_untrusted naming that interpreter. It does not follow the chain, so the follow-to-4-levels loop comes out of #313.
- "#!/usr/bin/env X" is unchanged: Ward walks env, (a12) Rule 1's built PATH confines X, and Ward does not resolve X ahead of exec.
- Tests. Reject: a script tool whose absolute interpreter is itself a "#!" script in a walked directory. Accept: a script tool whose interpreter is a regular binary in a walked directory."

Rule 3 (ELF RUNPATH residual) in DEC-262 (a12): not parsed by Ward; removing LD_PRELOAD and LD_LIBRARY_PATH is rule 1 (in #313). The note that a RUNPATH to a directory another user can write is a packaging defect outside AC2 is to be written in the WCLI-21 slice 3 ADR (the one that names DEC-262), not in this PR; WCLI-21 carries that obligation.

RULING DEC-262 (a14) from opum-doc, relayed by the leader, VERBATIM; implemented in #313 (finding 1 of the Opus review). Per the reviewer, "is env" is decided by EITHER the written basename or the final file's basename (multicall installs, aliases).

"- After a walked env, take the rest of the "#!" line as Linux passes it: everything after the interpreter path and its space or tab, as ONE argument. Refuse tool_untrusted, naming the line, unless it is a single bare command name: non-empty, printable ASCII, no space or tab inside it, no "/", no leading "-", no "=". env then resolves the bare name against (a12) Rule 1's built PATH.
- Reject tests: "env /abs/sh", "env -S PATH=/x sh", "env A=B sh", "env -i sh", and bare "env". Accept: "env sh", with sh in a walked directory.
- The reviewer's other findings are confirmed as (a12) as written; you're already sending them: the parent-PATH reject test proven red, a test seam for /usr/bin and /bin, EACCES → tool_untrusted, the shebang parser splitting on space and tab only with printable ASCII, and the RUNPATH residual in the ADR."

Landed: opum-ai/ward-cli#313 squashed to 00e8232 on origin/dev, after the Opus review APPROVE at 821caf62d0edf52eb6464c706e990b56d01e6878 (request-changes round 1 at 01e7454 answered by 244e5be and 821caf6, with DEC-262 a13 and a14 applied). Residuals recorded on WCLI-21 for the slice 3 ADR.
finalSummary: DEC-262 (a12), (a13) and (a14) implemented and landed as opum-ai/ward-cli#313 (squash 00e8232): built child environment, walked shebang interpreter refused if itself a script, env limited to one bare command name, tests both ways, after two Opus review rounds. Residuals are on WCLI-21.
